title: The in-between
hookLine: the Tibetan teachings on the bardos: dying, the clear light, becoming

lines: THE NEXT BAR NOT YET CAUGHT.
cards: High under a circus tent, a trapeze artist swings out on one bar. At the top of the arc, she lets go. For a moment she holds nothing at all: the old bar swinging away behind her, the new one still on its way.

Her whole act lives in that half second, because everything depends on what she does with empty hands. Tibetan teachers describe death, and much of life, as a moment like that. You first met their word for it in year one.

teach.b: First, the map. Bardo means in-between. Tibetan teachers describe several bardos, some in this life, like dreaming and meditation, and others that come with death.
Today, the passage through death as the teachings tell it: dying, the clear light, and becoming. Second, the bardo of dying.

teach.h: DYING: LAMPS GOING OUT ONE BY ONE.
teach.b: Teachers describe the body's powers withdrawing one by one, strength going, warmth fading, the senses dimming, like lamps going out room by room in a house at night.

They describe it calmly and in detail, so that someone who has heard it beforehand might recognize what's happening and not be afraid. At the very end, they say, a clear light dawns; that's tomorrow's lesson.
Third, the bardo of becoming. If the clear light isn't recognized, the teachings say, visions follow, which come soon.

teach.h: BECOMING: A FEATHER IN THE WIND.
teach.b: After them comes becoming: the mind, now without a body, pushed by old habits the way a feather is pushed by wind, is drawn toward a new birth.
The Bardo Thödol, read aloud beside the dead, speaks to the person at each step, reminding them: these appearances are your own mind. Fourth, why it's taught to the living.
Tibetan teachers say every in-between, falling asleep, waking up, the space between one thought and the next, is a small rehearsal.

teach.h: SMALL GAPS REHEARSE THE BIG ONE.
teach.b: What a person practices in the small gaps, steadiness, recognition, letting go, is what they'll have in the big one.
So the in-between isn't only a danger. It's an opening: with nothing held, for a moment, there's room to see clearly, and to catch the next bar well.

how: Tibetan Buddhists study the bardo teachings during life, practice with dreams and meditation as preparation, and read texts such as the Bardo Thödol aloud beside the dying and the dead to guide them through the in-between.

o: a Tibetan word for the afterlife's final judgment
the in-between: dying, the clear light, and becoming
a period of mourning when families wear white

p: lamps going out one by one
a feather pushed by the wind

s: the bardo teachings are only about what happens after death
dreaming, meditation and every gap in life are bardos too, small rehearsals.
the dying are taught the process beforehand so they won't be afraid
teachers describe it calmly and in detail so it can be recognized.
in the teachings, habit pushes the mind toward a new birth
like a feather pushed by the wind, in the bardo of becoming.

games.q: in the story the text tells, you've died, and strange visions rise up around you. what does the text read beside you keep saying?
o: run from them as fast as you can.
these appearances are your own mind.
choose the brightest vision and follow it.
games.why: the Bardo Thödol keeps reminding the one who has died that the visions are the mind's own display, to be recognized, not feared.

practice: Go gently, and bring to mind one in-between in your own life: between two jobs, two homes, two chapters, before a diagnosis and after it.
Notice how it feels in the body, then rest in the smallest in-between of all, the pause at the bottom of each out-breath, hands open.
If a loss is heavy on you today, you don't have to carry it alone: call or text 988 in the US, or reach local emergency help.

wordCard.voice: Bardo. The in-between: in Tibetan teaching, the passages of dying, the clear light, and becoming, and every gap in life where change can happen. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit antarabhava, the in-between existence, the Indian Buddhist term behind the Tibetan bardo.

carryVoice: Your line: in between. Empty hands, and for a moment, room to see. See you tomorrow.
